Th is appeal coming on for hearing this day, t h e cour  following:

ORDER This appeal has been filed being aggrieved with the award passed by the Claim Tribunal, Jabalpur in Accident Claim No.55/2017 dated 10.08.2018 by which the LRs of deceased have been allowed but observing the contributory negligence of the deceased in the incident 25% of the compensation amount has been reduced.

2. In nutshell the case before the Claim Tribunal was that the deceased Bake Singh was working as a constable in 6th Battalion of SAF Madhya Pradesh and earning Rs.40,000/- per month and on the date of incident dated 30.08.2016 after duty he was returning to his home at 12 PM in the night and reached near OFK Hospital, Kundam Road, the offending vehicle MP-19-CA- 0510 driven by respondent No.1 rashly and negligently hit the motorcycle of the deceased and as a result the deceased fell down from the vehicle and sustained injuries.
The deceased was brought for the treatment City Hospital Jabalpur.
During treatment he died and the information was sent to Police Station - Khamaria.
3. The case was registered against the respondent No.7, the driver of the offending vehicle MP-19-CA-0510 and after investigation, charge sheet was filed.
4. The claimants being the wife and children of the deceased has preferred the application under Section 166 of MV Act.

The Claim Tribunal on the recording the evidence and after hearing both the parties passed the impugned order and awarded an amount of Rs.30,26,932/- with the interest @
7% from the date of application till the amount deposited.

5. The Insurance Company being aggrieved with the award has filed this appeal under Section 173 (1) of the MV Act on the ground that the Tribunal has observed in para - 10 of the impugned award that deceased was found under the influence of Alcohol (Ex.P-4) and there was a head on collusion between the vehicles and on that basis the Claim Tribunal has assessed the contributory negligence of deceased 25% that ought to be 75%.

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for Insurance Company has further submitted that it is late night accident and as per the statement of the claimant witnesses it is clear that both the vehicles collide and the driver of the motorcycle was under the influence of Alcohol as per the MLC report (Ex.P-4) in that situation he was more liable for the accident if he would have been cautious and had not consumed the liquor the incident would have not been occurred.
Hence, prayed that the contributory negligence of the deceased be enhanced.
7. Learned counsel for the respondent Nos.1 to 6 has submitted that the Claim Tribunal has properly appreciated evident and after that passed the award, hence, no interference is required.
8. I have gone through the record.
As per the Ex.P-1 the police has filed the charge sheet against the respondent No.7 and from the Ex.P-2 the FIR that was lodged on the same day within five hours.
In which it is mentioned that the driver of the offending vehicle driving the four wheeler car with rash and negligent manner, hit the motorcycle and thus committed the incident.

9. Eye witness Satish Chourasiya (AW-2) has clearly stated that on the date of incident he was returning from Kundam on motorcycle along with his friend Abdul Waseem at 12:30 in the night,
when he reached near OFK Hosptial he saw the driver of the Car MP-19-CA-0510 over taking their motorcycle going to wrong side, hit the motorcycle as a result the driver of the motorcycle fell down and sustained injuries.
In the cross examination he has admitted that it was a head on collusion and nothing more has been brought on record against the deceased.

10. The Insurance Company has failed to demonstrate by filing the any FIR or proceeding initiated against the driver of the motorcycle i.e. deceased that on the basis of his contributory negligence any case was registered against the deceased.

On the point that when the doctor examined the deceased Bake Singh, the doctor has mentioned Alcoholic breath odor positive but doctor has not taken the blood sample of the deceased by examination of which it can be inferred that in what amount the Alcohol was present in the blood of the deceased.
11. After being that the Tribunal without proper evidence has assessed the liability of the deceased 25%.
On the basis of factual aspect no further contributory negligence can be inferred against the deceased driver of the motorcycle.
12. In this case the claimant has not preferred any appeal, hence, no interference is being made in the award but the appeal filed by the Insurance Company being devoid of merit and is dismissed.
13. With the copy of the order, the record of the Tribunal be returned back.
14. Record of this appeal be consigned to Record Room.

(DEVNARAYAN MISHRA) JUDGE DPS National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Bela Bai Maravi on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197210756/
